title: A design is a versioned durable aggregate that seats submit and read
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-8a6d6660c31c4e119f962d13e6f1505d (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF; children 2 and 3 build on it.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the design CONTRACT and its durable aggregate, plus the two command kinds and their roster backfill. No wrapper change, no mission change, no UI - those are children 2 and 3.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: `grep -rn 'design\.submit|DESIGN_STEP|designRevision' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns ZERO. Nothing exists between the Gate 1 approval and the decomposition run; the compiler seat plans straight from the approved contract. The gap is real in both directions.

THE SHAPE: aggregate `design:<goalId>` with VERSIONS. A revision carries five sections - screens/journey map (journey -> screens -> states), data model (entities, fields, relations), API surface (routes, payloads), component list, non-functional decisions (auth, accessibility, performance budgets) - plus open decisions for the human. Profile is the controlled one: TypeScript web app (React, Node, PostgreSQL).

TWO KINDS, DIFFERENT AUDIENCES, and this is the design decision worth stating: `design.submit` is a SEAT command (an agent submits a design) and `design.read` serves BOTH seats and the operator. So `design.submit` is NOT in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and is NOT MCP-excluded - it is the rare kind on this board that an agent SHOULD be able to call. Do not copy the human-only pattern from approval.decide/escalation.decide; copy the seat-facing pattern from planning.submit_decomposition instead.

ROSTER, traced from planning.submit_decomposition: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (kind, capability, family, PAYLOAD_KEYS), daemon-command-families.ts (the per-kind flag block at :83-94), daemon-command-registry.ts (`entryOf`, :205-212), mcp-tool-allowlist.ts (design.submit and design.read are SERVED over MCP, not excluded - they go in the served rosters), packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, and the GENERATED client via `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` (never hand-edited; it pins GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST, checked at client-compat.ts:169).

TWO PAYLOAD-KEY TEST TABLES must both gain rows and are invisible to a grep for the kind literal in production source: daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts (~:170-182) and daemon-command-registry.test.ts (~:197-203, plus the flat roster ~:283-300).
definitionOfDone: `design.submit` and `design.read` are published with the full roster backfill and a BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality test that enumerates the SERVED kinds from the dispatch seam and asserts equality with the advertised roster in both directions; verify by deleting each entry from each side in turn and confirming all four deletions go red.

Both kinds are SEAT-REACHABLE over MCP and are NOT in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS - assert that an agent-authenticated dispatch REACHES the handler, which is the opposite of the human-only kinds on this board. This arm exists because copying the approval.decide pattern here would silently make the design step unstaffable.

Three refusals with a closed code->layer map (the refusal factory takes no layer argument, so a call site cannot mint a disagreeing pair), each asserted with code AND layer: DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED (no approved Gate 1 revision), DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID (the exact-key section roster - assert an unknown extra key is REFUSED, not ignored), DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT (a stale expected version).

The aggregate `design:<goalId>` is durable and VERSIONED: submitting twice yields versions 1 and 2, both readable, and `design.read` returns the LATEST by default with the version number. Assert the second submit does not overwrite the first - a design whose history is lost cannot show the operator what changed.
The five sections plus the open-decisions list survive a write/read round trip byte-identically from a real store. Assert per section, not on the whole blob, so a dropped section names itself.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (packages/contracts and the generated client are touched, so the root lane is real evidence here).
taskRails: THESE ARE SEAT KINDS, NOT HUMAN GATES. `design.submit` must be callable by an agent over MCP; the human-only/MCP-excluded pattern used by approval.decide and escalation.decide is WRONG here and would make the design step unstaffable. Copy planning.submit_decomposition's seat-facing shape.
NO WRAPPER, MISSION OR UI CHANGE. Staffing the design step and carrying the design into the compiler mission is child 2; the Design tab is child 3.
NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client: run the generator and quote the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST.
VERSIONS ARE HISTORY, not a mutable field: a resubmit adds a version and never overwrites, because child 3 shows the operator which version the plan compiled against.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

EXPORTED, as the step named:
- AGGREGATE ID SHAPE: `DESIGN_AGGREGATE_PREFIX = "design:"`, `designAggregateId(goalId) -> `design:${goalId}``, `designRevisionEventId(goalId, version)`.
- RECORD VERSION: `DESIGN_REVISION_VERSION = "moe-design-revision/1"`, `DESIGN_REVISION_EVENT_TYPE = "DesignRevisionSubmitted"`, `DESIGN_PROFILE = "typescript-web-app/react-node-postgresql"` (SERVER-set, deliberately NOT a revision member - the profile is controlled, so a seat must not be able to present one).
- EXACT-ARITY ROSTERS: `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` = the 6 wire members (apiSurface, componentList, dataModel, nonFunctional, openDecisions, screens) and `DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS` = the FIVE sections alone, named apart from `openDecisions` so step 5(b) can assert per section and a dropped one names itself. Nested rosters are exact-arity too: DESIGN_JOURNEY_KEYS (journey, screens), DESIGN_SCREEN_KEYS (screen, states), DESIGN_ENTITY_KEYS (entity, fields, relations), DESIGN_ROUTE_KEYS (payload, route), DESIGN_NON_FUNCTIONAL_KEYS (accessibility, auth, performance = the auth/accessibility/performance-budget triple the description names).
- CLOSED CODE->LAYER MAP `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS`, `as const satisfies Readonly<Record<string, DesignLayer>>` over 3 layers (CONTRACT_AUTHORITY, LEDGER, REQUEST): DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED->CONTRACT_AUTHORITY, DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID->REQUEST, DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT->LEDGER, plus the three the store genuinely needs and can reach - DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT, DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED, DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE (all LEDGER). `DESIGN_CODES` is DERIVED at the roster site: `Object.freeze((Object.keys(DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS) as DesignCode[]).sort())` - never restated, so map and roster cannot disagree. `designRefusal(code, sourceCode?, sourceLayer?)` takes NO layer argument and reads `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS[code]`, so a call site cannot mint a disagreeing pair.
- DECODERS: `exactDesignRecord` (own enumerable string keys, exact arity, Object.prototype-or-null prototype only, rejects arrays and non-`value` descriptors), `decodeDesignRevision` (the ONE decode of seat bytes; copies every accepted member into fresh frozen records so a retained caller reference cannot mutate what is persisted), `decodeDesignRevisionBytes` (durable bytes -> revision via `decodeBoundedJsonBytes`, refusing DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED with the bounded-json code carried verbatim as `sourceCode` under sourceLayer "BOUNDED_JSON").

TWO DEFECTS I INTRODUCED AND FIXED BEFORE COMPLETING, both worth the reviewer's attention:
1. A RAW NUL BYTE (0x00) landed in the source at the `boundedDesignText` guard, which made the file read as BINARY to grep (`Binary file ... matches`, so every content grep over it silently degraded). Located by byte offset (`raw.find(b'\x00')` = 7059) and replaced with the escape `"�"`. `raw.count(b'\x00')` is now 0. Worth knowing: a NUL written into a .ts source does not fail tsc - it fails your ability to grep the file.
2. `decodeDesignRevisionBytes` originally passed `structuredClone(json.value)` to the decoder. Dropped: `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` already deep-freezes and its parser builds NULL-PROTOTYPE objects (bounded-json-parser.ts:87 `Object.create(null)`), which `exactDesignRecord` admits explicitly; the clone only added a prototype-changing hop between the two.

implementationPlan.description: THE SHAPE REFUSALS, in a new apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.test.ts. Assert each code maps to its declared layer and that the derived code roster equals the map's keys exactly. Then the decoder: DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID with its LAYER for a revision missing a section, for one carrying an UNKNOWN EXTRA key (refused, never ignored — silently dropping a member would let a seat believe it submitted something load-bearing), and for a section of the wrong type. Assert code AND layer on every arm (global rail 1): several layers can refuse a malformed payload, and the wrong one answering first keeps a test green while it stops testing its subject.

EVERY ARM ASSERTS CODE **AND** LAYER (global rail 1). 30 tests:

MAP AND ROSTER (5 arms + a 6-case table):
- The derived roster is compared against `Object.keys(DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS).sort()`, NOT against a list restated in the test. A restated roster is a second source of truth: deleting a code from production would shrink the map and the expectation together and the arm would never notice.
- `DESIGN_CODES.length > 0` guards the vacuous sweep (a roster that yielded zero codes would pass a `for` loop silently).
- 6-case `it.each` pinning each code to its declared layer, asserting `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS[code]` AND the minted `designRefusal(code).layer` - the constant and the factory both, since a factory that ignored the map would keep the constant arm green.
- "cannot be handed a layer by its call site": `designRefusal("DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID", "FOREIGN_CODE", "FOREIGN_LAYER")` still reports `layer === "REQUEST"` and parks the foreign pair in sourceCode/sourceLayer. This is the arm that would go red if someone re-added a layer parameter.
- Five sections + open-decisions: `DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS` has exactly 5 members and `[...DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS, "openDecisions"]` set-equals `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS`.

DECODER (a full-fixture admit + 6 missing-member cases + 6 wrong-type cases + 2 extra-key + 1 prototype + 3 bytes arms):
- MISSING SECTION: `it.each([...DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS])` deletes one member at a time - GENERATED FROM THE PRODUCTION ROSTER, so adding a seventh member to the contract automatically grows the sweep instead of leaving it stale. 6 cases actually generated (visible in the 30-test count; a sweep yielding zero would show as a lower total).
- UNKNOWN EXTRA KEY, refused NOT ignored, at both depths: top level (`telemetryBudget`) and nested inside a section (`nonFunctional.observability`), the nested arm also asserting `DESIGN_NON_FUNCTIONAL_KEYS` does not contain the key so it cannot pass by the roster quietly gaining it.
- WRONG TYPE per section, one case each, including the two that a lazy decoder gets wrong: a `dataModel` given a bare object instead of an array, and a `componentList` of objects instead of strings.
- INHERITED MEMBER: a revision whose `openDecisions` lives on the prototype is refused, so a `for...in`-shaped decoder could not pass.
- BYTES: JSON round trip; foreign bytes -> DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED at LEDGER; non-JSON bytes -> DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED at LEDGER with the bounded-json verdict carried verbatim (`sourceCode === "JSON_SYNTAX_INVALID"`, `sourceLayer === "BOUNDED_JSON"`). That last one is the arm that proves the delegated layer is COPIED rather than restated - the two-layer refusal keeps its provenance.
- Closed-map arm: a code outside the map has NO layer (`undefined`), so the lookup cannot silently default.

implementationPlan.description: THE VERSIONED AGGREGATE, in a new apps/daemon/src/design/design-store.ts (+ `.js` bridge). Append a revision to `design:<goalId>` using the store's expected-version commit (the expansion-request-commit.ts:83-118 shape), and read the LATEST with its version number. VERSIONS ARE HISTORY, NOT A MUTABLE FIELD: a resubmit APPENDS: version 1 stays readable after version 2 exists. That is not a nicety — child 3 (task-f3409f9a) shows the operator WHICH design version the plan compiled against, and child 2 (task-de059823) carries the design ref into the compiler mission; both are meaningless if history is overwritten. DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT is the stale-expected-version refusal, which is what makes two concurrent submits safe.
implementationPlan.note:
NEW apps/daemon/src/design/design-store.ts (211 lines) + design-records.ts (118 lines), each with its one-line `.js` bridge. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` EXIT=0; `src/design` suite still `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  30 passed (30)` EXIT=0.

THE APPEND. `submitDesignRevision` uses `store.commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs` with ONE leg on `design:<goalId>` at `expectedVersion`, event type `DesignRevisionSubmitted`, `domainSchemaVersion: "moe-design-revision/1"`, `eventId = design-revision-<version>-<goalId>`. It copies BOTH hazards from the expansion-request-commit.ts template: the thrown side (DurableStoreError EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT / DURABLE_ID_CONFLICT / IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT -> DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT with the store's own code carried as sourceCode under "DURABLE_STORE"; anything else -> DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE) AND the RETURNED side (`response.decision.effectDisposition !== "EFFECTS_COMMITTED"` -> DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT). The second is the one that matters: a fenced decision does not throw, so "the call returned" is how a resubmit would be reported as committed while history was never extended.

WHY A THIRD MODULE. design-records.ts holds the durable record codec (exact-key roster contractRef/goalRef/profile/projectId/revision/schemaVersion/submittedAt/version, byte-canonical encode built member-by-member in roster order, decode refusing a foreign schema/profile/version). Folding it into design-store.ts measured ~245 lines against the 250 target with no headroom; splitting is the rail-2 sanctioned move and keeps both files comfortably under. The VERSION IS A STORED FACT, not derived from array position: a projection that lost the aggregate sequence cannot silently renumber history.

THE APPROVAL GATE - and the one real design decision on this step, stated plainly because it is the part a reviewer should challenge.

Probe deleted (`rm -f apps/daemon/src/design/design-probe.test.ts`); `ls apps/daemon/src/design/` shows only the 7 intended files.

WHAT I BUILT INSTEAD, following the daemon's own precedent at http/document-coverage-read.ts:155-165 (the one place that already answers "is this goal's contract approved", and which reaches the gate-1 reader through the SOURCE-DOCUMENT digest, not a binding aggregate). `readApprovedDesignContract(store, {contractRef, goalRef, projectId})` composes THREE production surfaces and reimplements none:
  1. `admitProductContractRevisionRef(contractRef)` (@moe/core) - admits the triple;
  2. `readProductContractRevision(store, {projectId, ref})` -> the revision's `sourceDocumentDigests`;
  3. `validateRevisionProvenance(store, projectId, goalRef, digests)` (product-contract-provenance.ts:62) - proves the revision was authored against THIS GOAL's bound source document, which is the goal<->contract link this repo actually has;
  4. `readProductContractGate1Approval(store, {projectId, ref})` - proves a human granted Gate 1 over it.
Every refusal travels out as DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED with the delegated code AND layer copied verbatim into sourceCode/sourceLayer, so which authority answered is never lost.

THE CALLER NAMES A REF AND THAT GRANTS NOTHING. `contractRef` is typed `unknown` and is re-proved from durable state on every submit; step 3 above is specifically what stops a seat submitting a design for goal A while citing goal B's approved contract. I want this called out at review rather than buried: presenting the triple is a SELECTOR, not authority, and the arms in step 5 must show a foreign/unapproved triple refusing.
